edge.title: The caller who already knows you
edge.setup: Someone calls from 'your bank'. They know your name, the last four digits of your card, your recent transaction at a Koramangala restaurant. They're calling about a fraudulent charge they've blocked, and need to verify you're really you — an OTP is on its way.
edge.tell: Anyone asking you to read out a code is, by definition, not your bank.
move: Say: 'I'll call the number on the back of my card.' Then hang up and do exactly that.
Read the OTP message itself — it states the purpose. It usually says you are authorising the very transaction they claim to be blocking.
Knowing your details proves a leak happened, not that the caller is legitimate.
edge.why: Your personal data is already circulating — breaches, delivery apps, that form you filled at a mall kiosk. Scammers exploit a false equation in your head: 'knows private things' = 'is authorised'. An OTP exists precisely so that no one but you ever needs it.
edge.variants: Same shape: 'KYC expiring today', electricity-disconnection SMS with a callback number, fake customer-care numbers ranked high on search.

lens.name: Chesterton's fence
lens.one_line: Before removing something that looks pointless, find out why it was put there.
lens.detail: A rule, a process or a fence in a field that serves no visible purpose may be solving a problem you can't see precisely because it's being solved. The discipline isn't conservatism — it's the requirement to understand the original reason first, after which you may well still remove it, but now knowing the cost.
elsewhere: A weird approval step that quietly prevents a rare, expensive error.
Legacy code nobody dares delete, for reasons occasionally excellent.
A family practice that looks superstitious and encodes something practical.
lens.test: Do I understand why this exists? If not, I'm not yet qualified to remove it.
lens.today: The state government may relax tender norms because about ₹38,000 crore is owed to contractors (Times of India). Chesterton's fence asks what each norm was guarding before it is waved off: if the rules exist to keep bids honest, loosening them to clear a backlog could trade one problem for another. Same test applies to any rule you meet this week, from a society bylaw to a bank step you find annoying.

carry_over.prompt: You like a plot or flat in a layout, and every paper you are shown was handed over by the seller: what is the tell?
carry_over.answer: Every paper you are shown was handed over by the seller; none is a record you pulled yourself.
